reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a complete real inner-product space, let (Ω, μ) be a measurable probability space, let X : Ω → E, and let Σ be a continuous linear endomorphism of E. For ω∈Ω, define Rω : E→E by Rω(y)=⟪X(ω),y⟫X(ω). Assume ‖X(ω)‖=1 for every ω, the operator-valued map ω↦Rω is Bochner integrable, and ∫Ω Rω dμ(ω)=Σ. Then Σ is self-adjoint, ‖Σ‖≤1, ∫Ω(Rω−Σ)² dμ(ω)=Σ−Σ², and ‖Σ−Σ²‖≤2‖Σ‖.
objects: A complete real inner-product space E; a measurable space Ω; a probability measure μ; a sample map X; and a continuous linear operator Σ.
domains: E is complete over ℝ; μ is a probability measure on Ω; X maps Ω to E; Σ is a continuous real-linear endomorphism.
quantifiers: All spaces, measures, maps, and operators are universal theorem parameters; the unit-norm premise holds for every ω.
assumptions: Pointwise unit norm, Bochner integrability of the self rank-one operator map, and equality of its Bochner integral with Σ.
conclusion: Σ is self-adjoint, has norm at most one, has centered operator second moment Σ-Σ², and satisfies ‖Σ-Σ²‖≤2‖Σ‖.
scopes: Operator powers are composition powers and all integrals are operator-valued Bochner integrals; no finite-dimensionality or repeated samples occur.
constant_dependencies: The constants 1 and 2 are absolute and dimension-free.
